global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of guests who must be placed in a single row. This tells the solver how many distinct people appear in the lineup and that each must be placed exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of friendship ties among the guests. Each tie is an undirected link between two guests that may contribute to crossings between left and right sides at any gap in the row.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (names or numeric IDs) of every guest to be ordered. These are the items to be permuted left-to-right when evaluating how many friendships cross each gap.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship tie: the first guest in this friendship pair. Together with 'guest_b' it defines an undirected friendship that may cross a gap if the two guests are placed on opposite sides.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the friendship tie: the second guest in this pair. The unordered pair (guest_a, guest_b) represents a friendship link whose crossing behavior is counted between left and right groups in the lineup.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers that must be placed in a single linear order on the rack; this equals the length of the ordering (permutation).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of network cables connecting pairs of servers. Each cable is an undirected connection that may span a rack gap and contribute to cut sizes.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of server identifiers (labels) to be arranged along the rack. Every identifier appears exactly once in the final order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint server identifier of a particular network cable. Together with 'v' it specifies an undirected cable between two servers.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint server identifier of the same network cable. The unordered pair (u, v) means a cable running between these two servers.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of books that must be placed in one continuous linear order on the shelf; this tells you how many positions the ordering will contain.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected cross-reference links between books (each link is a reference that can contribute to a cut when the shelf is split).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of unique identifiers for each book (each identifier corresponds to one volume that must appear exactly once in the shelf order); these identifiers are used by the edges to specify which books are linked.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint book of a single cross-reference link; paired with the 'v' field to indicate which two books are connected by that reference (an undirected link).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint book of the same cross-reference link; together with 'u' it defines a reference whose crossing behavior across any shelf gap contributes to the cut size.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of performers that must be placed once each in the single parade line.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of past collaborative ties (undirected links) between performers; each such tie is a pair that may ‘stretch’ across a gap in the parade order.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An array of identifiers (names or IDs) for every performer to be ordered in the parade; each identifier appears exactly once and must be placed in the final linear order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaborative tie: the identifier of the first performer in this collaboration pair (must match an identifier from performer_list).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the collaborative tie: the identifier of the second performer in this collaboration pair (must match an identifier from performer_list).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of exhibits that must be placed in a single linear order along the corridor. This tells the solver how many positions the curator must fill.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of thematic links between exhibits. Each link connects two exhibits and may contribute to cut sizes when the lineup is split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (labels or names) used for each exhibit. These identifiers are referenced when describing which two exhibits a thematic link connects.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a thematic link: the identifier of the first exhibit involved in this link. Order is not significant (links are undirected), but this must match an entry from exhibit_ids.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a thematic link: the identifier of the second exhibit in this link. Together with exhibit_a it specifies which two exhibits are thematically connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pallets that must be placed in a single file. This is the count of distinct items the foreman must order so every pallet appears exactly once in the line.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of dependency lines (ties) between pallets. Each dependency is an undirected connection whose crossings contribute to cut sizes when the pallets are ordered.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each pallet to be ordered. These identifiers are the distinct labels the foreman will arrange into a permutation when evaluating cut sizes between adjacent positions.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a dependency line: the identifier of the first pallet involved in this tie. Together with the other endpoint it defines a connection whose crossing contributes to cut sizes depending on their relative order.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a dependency line: the identifier of the second pallet in this tie. The pair (pallet_endpoint_1, pallet_endpoint_2) denotes an undirected dependency between two pallets.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students the teacher must line up for the photo. This is the size of the lineup and equals the number of nodes in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of friendship connections among the students. Each friendship is an undirected connection that can contribute to a cut between a front group and back group.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers or labels for each student (e.g., names or numbers). These are the items to be arranged in a single linear order for the photo.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship: the identifier of the first student in this friendship pair. Along with student_b, this defines an undirected friendship edge that may cross a cut in the lineup.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a friendship: the identifier of the second student in this friendship pair. student_a and student_b together specify which two students are friends.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct songs the band must place into a single playlist. This equals the number of nodes in the graph; the final playlist must be a permutation that contains each of these songs exactly once (no omissions or repeats).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected musical transitions (edges) between pairs of songs. Each transition represents a meaningful link between two songs that will contribute to cut sizes when the playlist is split at any gap.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each song (node) referenced in the setup. Use these IDs when specifying the playlist order; each ID corresponds to one song and must appear exactly once in the ordering.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a musical transition: the identifier of one song in this linked pair. Together with the other endpoint, it defines an undirected transition between two songs. If the two songs fall on different sides of a playlist gap, this transition increases that gap's cut count by 1.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the musical transition: the identifier of the second song in the linked pair. The pair (song_u, song_v) is an undirected edge representing a link that may cross any gap in the playlist.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments that must be hung in one single sequence on the rail; each garment appears exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of stylistic links (pairs of garments that are considered ‘connected’ by style) whose crossings we count when evaluating cuts between positions on the rail.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of the unique identifiers for each garment (these identifiers are the items to be permuted into a single linear hanging order).

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a stylistic link: the identifier of the first garment in this linked pair. If this garment is placed left of a split while its partner is right, this link contributes to that cut.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the stylistic link: the identifier of the second garment in the pair. Together with the first endpoint it defines a connection whose crossing is counted at any split that separates them.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of scenes that must be placed into a single continuous sequence. Use this to know how many scene positions the editor will order (the permutation length).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of narrative threads (undirected links) that connect pairs of scenes. This is the number of scene-to-scene connections whose crossings at splices are counted when evaluating cut sizes.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each scene (one per scene). These labels are used when specifying the order and when referring to endpoints of narrative threads.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint scene identifier for a narrative thread. Together with 'scene_b' this denotes an undirected link between two scenes whose placement may cause a thread to cross an edit.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint scene identifier for the same narrative thread. The pair (scene_a, scene_b) marks two scenes connected by a thread; whether the thread crosses a splice depends on their relative order in the final sequence.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of furniture pieces that must be placed in a single straight line in the truck. This tells the solver how many distinct positions the permutation must contain (no piece can be skipped or repeated).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pairwise packing interdependencies between pieces (connections). Each dependency is an undirected link that can contribute to the crossing count at a split if its two endpoint items lie on different sides of that split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each piece of furniture (one per item). The final ordering must be a permutation of these identifiers; edges reference these ids to indicate which pieces are connected.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a packing dependency: the identifier of the first furniture piece involved in this connection. When ordering, if this item appears before a split and the paired item appears after, this connection counts toward that split's crossing total.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a packing dependency: the identifier of the second furniture piece in this connection. Together with 'item_a', it defines a pair whose relative positions determine whether the dependency crosses a given split.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of tasks that must appear exactly once in the single ordered checklist. This is the size of the list you will arrange to minimize the peak number of dependencies crossing any cut.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dependency links (undirected connections) between pairs of tasks. Each such link may contribute to the cut count when its two endpoint tasks lie on opposite sides of a split in the order.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (names or numeric IDs) of all tasks to be placed in the checklist. Every identifier here must appear exactly once in the final ordering and is referenced by dependency pairs below.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint task of a dependency link. Must be one of the identifiers from the task_ids list; paired with task_v to describe a dependency that can span a cut.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint task of a dependency link. Together with task_u it defines an undirected dependency that contributes to the crossing count if the two tasks lie on different sides of any split in the ordered checklist.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of talks to schedule in one uninterrupted program. This equals the number of nodes in the graph and determines how many talks must appear in the single linear order.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of audience-members (or distinct interest-pairs) who care about exactly two talks, i.e., the number of edges in the graph. Each edge represents one person whose interests connect the two endpoint talks and who would have to cross the break if those talks fall on opposite sides.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for all talks (the node labels). The solution is a permutation of these talk_ids representing the single-room schedule; cuts are considered between consecutive positions in that order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint talk identifier for this audience overlap (one of the two talks the audience member is interested in). Refers to an entry in talk_ids.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint talk identifier for this audience overlap (the second talk the same audience member is interested in). Together with talk_a, it defines the pair of talks linked by that audience member.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of plants that must be placed in the single flower bed. This equals the number of vertices in the graph and the length of the 'nodes' list; every plant must appear exactly once in the final ordering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of root interactions (undirected edges) between plants. Each interaction is a pairwise connection that can cross a cut and contribute 1 to the cut size whenever its two endpoint plants lie on opposite sides of the split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of unique identifiers (names or IDs) for the plants to arrange. These are the vertices of the graph; the solver will produce a permutation of these identifiers as the planting order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a root interaction: the identifier of one plant connected by this edge. Matches an entry in 'plant_ids'. Because connections are undirected, this is just one end of the unordered pair.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same root interaction: the identifier of the second plant in the pair. Together with 'plant_u' it defines an undirected root connection that contributes to any cut separating the two plants.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct procedural steps in the recipe. Each step is a node that must appear exactly once in the final linear ordering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected links representing shared-ingredient relationships. Each link denotes that the two connected steps both use (or touch) the same ingredient, and such a link can contribute to a cut when one of its steps is placed before the cut and the other after.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (names or numeric IDs) for every recipe step. These are the nodes to be permuted into a single sequence whose worst ingredient-crossing cut-size should be minimized.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an ingredient-sharing link: the identifier of the first step that uses the shared ingredient. The link is undirected, so this is just one of the two steps connected by that ingredient.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the ingredient-sharing link: the identifier of the second step that uses the shared ingredient. Together with 'step_a', this pair indicates an ingredient that could be carried across a cut between steps.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of landmarks (attractions/sites) that must be arranged into a single linear tour; this is the number of positions in the route the planner will produce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected connections (paths) between landmarks on the map; each path may contribute to the crossing count at a split where one endpoint is already visited and the other is still ahead.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of landmark identifiers (names or numeric IDs) that will be permuted into the tour order; the relative order of these identifiers determines which connections are counted as crossings at each visited/unvisited cut.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint landmark for a specific undirected path; together with 'v' this defines a connection that will be counted whenever the tour split places this endpoint on the visited side and the other on the unvisited side.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint landmark for the undirected path paired with 'u'; the pair (u,v) represents a direct link whose presence affects the cut size when the route separates its endpoints.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of accessories to arrange along the single straight shelf; equals the number of nodes in the graph and determines how many distinct positions the buyer must fill.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of style links (pairings) between accessories; each link is an undirected connection that will contribute to a cut whenever its two endpoints lie on opposite sides of a shelf divider.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of accessory identifiers (labels) used to name each item on the shelf; these IDs are referenced when specifying style pairings and when describing the final linear order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint accessory identifier of a style pairing: the first item in the linked pair. Used together with 'v' to define a connection whose crossing of a divider increases the cut count.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint accessory identifier of the style pairing: the second item in the linked pair. Paired with 'u' to indicate the two linked accessories whose relative positions affect cut sizes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students to be placed in a single continuous seating row. This is the count of distinct people that must each appear exactly once in the arrangement used to evaluate cut sizes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected social links (friendships or ties) between students. Each link connects two students and contributes to cut counts when its endpoints fall on different sides of a seat boundary.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of student identifiers (names or IDs) corresponding to the students being seated. These are the items to permute into a single linear order when computing how many friendships cross each boundary.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a social link: the identifier of one student involved in this friendship. Together with 'v' this defines an undirected tie that may span a seating boundary.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a social link: the identifier of the second student in this friendship. The pair (u,v) describes a single undirected social connection counted when it crosses a left/right cut.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct shuttle stops that must be listed exactly once in the single loop ordering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected passenger trip connections (edges) between stops; each edge represents a passenger travel demand between two stops that can contribute to a cut.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of the identifiers for each shuttle stop (stop codes or names) that will be permuted into the single loop order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint stop identifier of this passenger trip connection. Together with stop_b it defines a trip demand; if stop_a and stop_b lie on opposite sides of a cut in the ordering, this trip counts toward that cut's size.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint stop identifier of this passenger trip connection. The pair (stop_a, stop_b) denotes an undirected trip between two stops that may cross cuts in the loop ordering.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of paintings to place along the single exhibition wall; every painting must appear exactly once in the final linear sequence.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of thematic connections (story-ties) between pairs of paintings; each connection links two paintings whose relationship can contribute to a crossing at a gap.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of unique identifiers (labels or indices) for each painting in the collection; these identifiers are used to define where connections attach and to specify the ordering.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a thematic connection: the identifier of the first painting in this connection pair (must match an entry from painting_ids).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a thematic connection: the identifier of the second painting in this connection pair (must match an entry from painting_ids).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of neighborhood trees that must be placed in the single straight lineup along the promenade. This is the count of distinct trees to order, and every tree must appear exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of irrigation pipes (undirected connections) between pairs of trees. Each pipe connects two trees and contributes to cut counts if its endpoints lie on different sides of a slice through the row.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the trees (labels or indices). These IDs are used to refer to individual trees when specifying which trees are connected by irrigation pipes and when producing an ordering of the trees along the promenade.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint tree of a specific irrigation pipe. Together with 'v' (tree_v), it denotes an undirected pipe between two trees; the order of u and v does not imply direction.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint tree of the same irrigation pipe. The pair (tree_u, tree_v) specifies which two trees are joined by that pipe and therefore which edge contributes to cuts when those trees lie on opposite sides of a slice.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct books that must be placed on the single shelf; equals the number of nodes in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of thematic cross-reference connections between books; equals the number of undirected edges in the graph.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (labels or indices) for each book; these identifiers are used when listing cross-reference pairs.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a cross-reference: the identifier of the first book in this cross-reference pair (from book_ids). As the graph is undirected, this is one of the two books connected by the thematic link.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a cross-reference: the identifier of the second book in this cross-reference pair (from book_ids). Together with book_u it specifies an undirected link between two books.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of visiting booths that must be placed in a single linear order along the fair walkway — i.e., the number of graph vertices to permute (each booth appears exactly once).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vendor collaborations (undirected connections) between booths — i.e., the number of graph edges whose crossings contribute to cut sizes when the booths are ordered.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (labels) for all booths. These are the labels you must arrange into a single visiting sequence; each identifier corresponds to one booth vertex in the graph.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaboration: the identifier of the first booth involved in this undirected vendor collaboration (edge). Paired with 'v' to indicate the two booths whose collaboration may cross a cut.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the collaboration: the identifier of the second booth involved in this undirected vendor collaboration (edge). Together with 'u' it specifies a collaboration that can contribute to cut sizes depending on their ordering.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of photo frames that must be placed in a single linear order along the mantel. This equals the length of the final arrangement.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of visual ties (connections) between frames. Each tie links two distinct frames and contributes to cut counts when the two frames lie on opposite sides of a break.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers (labels) for every photo frame to be ordered. Every identifier here must appear exactly once in the final permutation and must match the endpoints used in the tie list.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint identifier of a visual tie: the label of one frame connected by this tie. The pair (frame_u, frame_v) denotes an undirected connection; order is irrelevant.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint identifier of the visual tie: the label of the second frame connected by this tie. Together with frame_u it defines a single undirected tie counted once when it crosses a mantel break.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of task cards on the project board that must be placed into a single sequence. This equals the length of the final ordering and should match the number of identifiers in "nodes."

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dependency links between tasks. Each link connects two task cards; when the sequence is split, a link contributes to the cut if its two endpoint tasks lie on different sides of the split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for every task card on the board. Each identifier must appear exactly once in the output ordering.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint task identifier of a dependency link. Together with "v" it specifies a link between two tasks; the order here is not directional for cut counting.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint task identifier of the same dependency link specified with "u." If this task and the "u" task end up on different sides of a split, that link contributes to the split's crossing count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct artworks (pieces) that must be placed in a single linear sequence along the gallery wall.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of artistic pairings (undirected connections) between artworks; each pairing links two pieces and contributes to cut counts depending on their relative positions.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers (labels or names) for every artwork to be arranged; these identifiers are used by the pairings to indicate which pieces are connected.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a pairing: the identifier of the first artwork involved in this artistic connection (must match an entry in artwork_ids).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same pairing: the identifier of the second artwork involved in this artistic connection (must match an entry in artwork_ids).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of storefronts (cafés and shops) that must be placed into one linear sequence along the block. This tells the solver how many distinct venues to order.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of loyalty ties between pairs of storefronts. Each tie represents a potential pedestrian crossover; the objective is to order stores to minimize the maximum number of ties crossing any split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for every storefront (names or IDs). Each identifier corresponds to one node that must appear exactly once in the final linear arrangement.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a loyalty tie: the identifier of the first storefront in this undirected pair. Used together with the other endpoint to represent a single customer-traffic link that may cross a split.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the loyalty tie: the identifier of the second storefront in this undirected pair. The pair (endpoint_store_a, endpoint_store_b) denotes a bidirectional link counted when it spans a cut between earlier and later stores in the sequence.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of students to seat along the single long bench — i.e., the number of vertices in the friendship graph. The final ordering must place each of these students exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of friendship links (undirected edges) between students. Each friendship connects two students and can contribute to the crossing count at a bench split if the two students end up on different sides of that split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (labels) for the students to be seated. These identifiers are used when specifying friendships and when producing the linear seating order (a permutation of these identifiers).

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship link: the identifier of one student in the pair. Since friendships are undirected, the pair (student_a, student_b) represents a single mutual link regardless of order.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a friendship link: the identifier of the second student in the pair. Together with student_a this defines a friendship that may cross a seating split depending on their positions in the ordering.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of packages that must be placed in a single serial order on the conveyor. This is the count of distinct package identifiers that will appear in the sequence; every package must be included exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of routing ties connecting pairs of packages. Each routing tie links two packages and may cross any gap between earlier and later packages in an ordering; this number equals the count of such ties listed.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An explicit list of the package identifiers (labels) that are to be arranged on the conveyor. These identifiers are the elements to be permuted left-to-right when evaluating cut crossings.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint package for this routing tie. Together with the other endpoint, it defines an undirected tie between two packages whose crossing relative to any gap is counted.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint package for this routing tie. The pair (tie_package_a, tie_package_b) represents a routing connection that may straddle a split between earlier and later packages in an order.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of brochure sections (panels) that must be placed exactly once in a single linear layout; this is the length of the ordering you will produce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected cross-reference links between sections; each link connects two sections and contributes to cut sizes when the ordering splits them.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the brochure sections (panel labels) that can be permuted; these are the items to order left-to-right.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a cross-reference link: the identifier of one section that is linked to another section. Because links are undirected, this is one member of the linked pair.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a cross-reference link: the identifier of the section paired with section_a. When the layout has section_a on the left of a cut and section_b on the right, this link contributes to that cut's crossing count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potted plants you must place in a single row on the balcony — i.e., the number of vertices in the layout problem.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of drip lines (hoses) that connect pairs of pots — i.e., the number of undirected edges between pots.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An explicit list of identifiers for each pot (labels you will use to refer to pots when specifying drip-line connections and when describing an ordering).

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint pot for this drip line — one of the two pots connected by the hose (order is irrelevant since the drip lines are undirected).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint pot for this drip line — the second pot connected by the hose (paired with pot_a to specify the connection).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of playlists that must be placed into one linear sequence — i.e., the number of nodes in the graph. Every playlist counted here must appear exactly once in the final ordering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of undirected playlist pairs that are reported to share at least one track (the number of edges). Each listed edge indicates there exists at least one track present in both playlists; if two playlists share multiple tracks they are represented here by a single listed pair unless the input provides duplicates.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An array of identifiers (names or unique IDs) for each playlist. These are the items to be permuted into a single ordering — the sequence must include each identifier from this list exactly once.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an undirected edge: the identifier of a playlist that shares at least one track with the playlist specified in the paired field 'v'.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an undirected edge: the identifier of a playlist that shares at least one track with the playlist specified in 'u'. The unordered pair (u,v) denotes a shared-track relationship that will count toward a cut if the two playlists lie on opposite sides of a split.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct museum audio guides to be arranged in the single onboarding sequence. Each guide corresponds to one node that must appear exactly once in the final permutation used to evaluate cuts.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected cross-links (relationships or references) between pairs of guides. Each link contributes to the cut count whenever its two endpoint guides lie on opposite sides of a split in the sequence.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for all guides (e.g., numeric IDs or short labels). These are the items to be ordered; each identifier denotes one node in the graph used to compute cut sizes.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint guide of an undirected link. Together with 'v' this specifies a cross-link; if guide_u is placed before a split and guide_v after it, that link increases the cut size at that split by 1.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint guide of an undirected link. Paired with 'u' to define a relation between two guides that may contribute to crossings when the onboarding list is split.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of research samples (test tubes) that must be placed once in a single linear order along the bench.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of contamination-risk connections (undirected links) between pairs of samples; each such link represents a potential crossing to minimize.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the individual research samples; these labels are used to refer to samples when specifying contamination-risk links and when building an ordering.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint sample of a contamination-risk link: the first sample in the pair that is connected (links are undirected, so this is one of the two samples involved).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint sample of the contamination-risk link: the second sample in the connected pair (complements 'sample_a' to define the undirected risk connection).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recipe cards that must be placed into the single stacked sequence; every card is included exactly once and this is the count of those cards.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of ingredient-overlap links between cards. Each overlap represents a shared ingredient that forms an undirected connection between two recipe cards and can contribute to the cut size when the two cards lie on different sides of a cut.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each recipe card (e.g., names or IDs). These are the items to be ordered in the stack; each identifier corresponds to one physical recipe card.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a shared-ingredient link: the identifier of the first recipe card in this overlapping pair. Together with 'card_b' this denotes two cards that share an ingredient.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a shared-ingredient link: the identifier of the second recipe card in this overlapping pair. The unordered pair (card_a, card_b) represents one shared-ingredient connection that may cross a cut depending on their order in the stack.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of mobile devices to place in the single-file train. This equals the length of the ordering you must produce (every device appears exactly once).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of active Bluetooth pairings between devices. These pairings are the undirected connections whose crossings across any split contribute to the cut size.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each mobile device to be arranged. Use these identifiers when specifying endpoints of pairings and when constructing the linear order (train).

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint device identifier (from device_ids) of a Bluetooth pairing. Together with 'device_v' it defines an undirected pairing whose endpoints contribute to cut counts when separated by a split.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint device identifier (from device_ids) of a Bluetooth pairing. The pairing (device_u, device_v) is undirected and counts as crossing any split that places its endpoints on different sides.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mailboxes in the neighborhood that must be arranged into a single linear sequence; this is the count of nodes that the permutation must include.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct delivery routes connecting pairs of mailboxes; each route is an undirected connection between two mailboxes and contributes to cut sizes when its endpoints lie on opposite sides of a cut.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An explicit list of the mailbox identifiers (labels or IDs). Each identifier names one mailbox that must appear exactly once in the final ordering; endpoints in the route list refer to these identifiers.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint mailbox identifier of a delivery route; together with 'mailbox_endpoint_v' it defines a route between two mailboxes. When ordering, a route counts toward a cut if this mailbox is on the left and the other endpoint is on the right (or vice versa).

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint mailbox identifier of the same delivery route. Pairs of (mailbox_endpoint_u, mailbox_endpoint_v) describe all routes whose crossings across cuts determine cut sizes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of speakers that must be placed into a single linear schedule order. This is the count of distinct speakers appearing in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of past collaboration links between speakers. Each link is an undirected connection whose crossings we aim to minimize when ordering the schedule.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An array of the speaker identifiers (IDs or names). Every identifier here must appear exactly once in the final schedule and is used as endpoints in the collaboration links.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaboration link: the identifier of a speaker involved in this collaboration. In each collaboration pair, 'speaker_u' together with 'speaker_v' denotes an undirected link between those two speakers.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a collaboration link: the identifier of the second speaker in this collaboration. 'speaker_u' and 'speaker_v' together define a single undirected collaboration that may cross a schedule pause.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of decorative tiles that must be placed in a single straight row for the backsplash; this is the count of distinct tiles, each used exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected grout channels (connections) between pairs of tiles; each channel links two tiles and can contribute to a cut when the row is split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers (labels) for every tile available. Each identifier uniquely refers to one tile and will be placed once in the final linear ordering.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint tile identifier for a specific grout channel; together with 'tile_endpoint_b' it denotes a connection between two tiles that counts toward any split separating those tiles.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint tile identifier for the grout channel; paired with 'tile_endpoint_a' to describe the two tiles linked by that channel.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct products that must be placed once each along the single shelf row. This determines how many positions the ordering must cover.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise connections (links) between products. Each connection represents a relationship that contributes to a busy boundary if its two products end up on opposite sides of a shelf break.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (labels) for each product to place on the shelf. These IDs are used when listing connections so a solver knows which products are linked.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a connection: the identifier of the first product in this linked pair. If product_a and product_b are separated by a cut in the ordering, this connection counts toward that cut's size.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a connection: the identifier of the second product in this linked pair. Together with product_a, it defines a link that may cross a shelf break and increase the busiest boundary count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of guests who must be seated along the single long table; i.e., the count of unique people to place in one linear seating order (each guest gets exactly one seat).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected social ties (friendships/acquaintances) among the guests; each tie is an edge that can contribute to crossing counts when its endpoints fall on different sides of a seating split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of guest identifiers (names or numeric IDs) that names every person to be seated. These identifiers are referenced by the relationships; the seating solution must place each identifier exactly once in a single permutation along the table.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a social tie: the identifier of the first guest in this relationship (must match an entry in guest_list). In cut counting an edge contributes if guest_a and guest_b are on opposite sides of a seating gap.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the social tie: the identifier of the second guest in this relationship (must match an entry in guest_list). Edges are undirected, so (guest_a, guest_b) is the same tie as (guest_b, guest_a).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of songs to place in the single linear playlist. Every song must appear exactly once in the setlist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise song connections (undirected pairings) that represent transitions or relationships between two songs. Each pairing can be cut if its two songs lie on opposite sides of a split in the playlist.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for all songs (IDs or titles) that must be ordered. These identifiers are used by the pairings to refer to which two songs are connected.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a song pairing: the identifier of the first song in this undirected connection. If this song and song_b are separated by a split in the playlist, this pairing contributes to that split's cut size.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the song pairing: the identifier of the second song in this undirected connection. Together with song_a, it defines a pair whose membership on opposite sides of a playlist divide increases the cut count by one.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct prep ingredients that must be placed once in a single straight lineup along the kitchen counter. This is the number of items to order.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected ingredient-pair interactions. Each interaction is a pair of ingredients whose relationship contributes to a cut when the two are separated by any divider in the lineup.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each ingredient (names or numeric IDs). These are the items to be permuted into the lineup; each identifier appears exactly once in the final order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an interacting ingredient pair: the identifier of the first ingredient in this interaction. Together with 'ingredient_b' it defines an undirected pair whose separation across a divider increments that divider's split tally.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an interacting ingredient pair: the identifier of the second ingredient in this interaction. The pair (ingredient_a, ingredient_b) is unordered and counts as a single interaction that may be split by a lineup divider.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of crates that must be placed into a single-file sequence at the dock; equals the number of distinct crate identifiers to order.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of physical connections (handles or straps) between pairs of crates; each connection links two crates and contributes to cut counts when the two crates are separated by a split in the sequence.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (labels) for every crate present at the dock; these are the items you must arrange into a single permutation so each identifier appears exactly once.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a connection: the identifier of the first crate attached by this handle/strap. In the undirected scenario it is just one of the two crates that the connection joins.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a connection: the identifier of the second crate attached by this handle/strap. Together with crate_end_a this defines a single undirected link between two crates.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of paintings to be hung in a single linear sequence along the gallery wall. This tells the solver how many distinct items must appear once in the order.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of thematic links (connections) between paintings. Each link is a relationship that, if its endpoints lie on opposite sides of a cut in the hanging order, contributes to that cut's size.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of unique identifiers for each painting. These IDs are the elements to be permuted into a single ordering; no ID is repeated and every ID must appear exactly once in the hanging arrangement.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a thematic link: the identifier of one painting involved in this connection. Together with the other endpoint, it defines a pair whose separation by a wall cut contributes to the cut size.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the thematic link: the identifier of the second painting in this connection. The unordered pair (painting_a, painting_b) represents a single thematic link between those two paintings.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of family photographs to place in a single continuous album sequence; defines the length of the permutation the solver must produce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of relationship links between photos (e.g., who appears with whom or narrative connections). Each link connects two photos and may contribute to a cut if its endpoints fall on opposite sides of a split in the ordering.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of unique photo identifiers (labels) that must each appear exactly once in the final linear album order; the solver arranges these IDs to minimize the maximum number of links crossing any split between earlier (left) and later (right) photos.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a relationship link: the identifier of the first photo connected by this link. When evaluating a candidate ordering, this photo's position is compared to the other endpoint to determine whether the link crosses a given split.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the relationship link: the identifier of the second photo connected by this link. Together with the 'photo_a_id', it defines a connection that may cross an ordering split if the two photos lie on opposite sides.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of recorded segments (clips) that must be placed once each in a single linear episode order. This is the count of items to permute.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of editorial connections between segments. Each connection represents a link (transition, reference, or dependency) between two clips that can contribute to the number of crossing links at an edit point.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the individual segments (clip labels or IDs). These are the tokens you will order; every edge references two of these identifiers.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an editorial connection: the identifier of the first segment involved in this link. Connections are undirected, so this is one of the two segment IDs that, if separated by an edit point, will count toward that cut's crossing number.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the editorial connection: the identifier of the second segment involved in this link. Together with 'segment_a' it defines a pair whose separation by an edit increases the crossing count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of seedlings you must plant in the single row along the garden bed — i.e., how many distinct specimens need to be placed (each used exactly once).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered influencing pairs: how many distinct pairs of seedlings have a mutual influence that counts if they end up on opposite sides of any spot in the row.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers (names or numeric IDs) for each seedling to be placed in the row; these are the items you will permute when deciding planting order.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an influencing pair: the identifier of the first seedling in this unordered pair that will contribute to a cut if planted on the opposite side of a spot from seedling_b.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the influencing pair: the identifier of the second seedling in this unordered pair that will contribute to a cut if planted on the opposite side of a spot from seedling_a.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of services that must be placed into the single sequential boot order; each service appears exactly once in the sequence.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dependency links (visualized as ropes) between pairs of services; each such link contributes to the cut size when its two endpoint services lie on opposite sides of a cut in the boot sequence.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An array of service identifiers (names or IDs) that will be ordered for startup; the solver must produce a permutation of these identifiers representing the boot sequence.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint service of a dependency link (one end of a rope). Together with 'v' it defines a rope between two services; the rope is counted at any cut where service_u has been started but service_v has not, or vice versa.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint service of a dependency link (the other end of the rope). Paired with 'u' to specify an undirected dependency whose cross-cut occurrences contribute to cut sizes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of railcars to place in a single train order. Use this to know how many car identifiers to expect and to ensure every car is placed exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of couplings between cars. Each coupling is an undirected connection between two cars that can contribute to the cut size if its cars lie on different sides of a split.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of the identifiers for every railcar (each used once in the ordering). These are the labels you will permute to form the train lineup.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one end of a coupling: the first car involved in this coupling. Paired with 'car_b' to describe an undirected coupling between two specific cars.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other end of a coupling: the second car involved in this coupling. Together with 'car_a' it specifies which two cars are connected by this coupling.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of parcels that must be queued on the conveyor (each parcel appears exactly once in the final continuous lineup).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of paired delivery relations: each represents a matched pair of parcels whose connection contributes to cut sizes when split across a belt point.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers used for each parcel (labels for the boxes). These IDs reference parcels when specifying which parcels form a matched pair.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one parcel in a matched delivery pair; this must match one of the entries in 'parcel_ids'.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other parcel in the matched delivery pair; paired with 'parcel_a' and also must appear in 'parcel_ids'.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of chapters to place in the table of contents. This is the number of nodes in the graph; each chapter must appear exactly once in the final linear ordering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cross-reference links between chapters. Each link is an undirected reference that may contribute to cut sizes when the two linked chapters fall on opposite sides of a division in the ordering.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for every chapter (node) that must be ordered. These identifiers are used to refer to chapters when describing cross-reference pairs and evaluating cuts between earlier and later chapters.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a cross-reference: the identifier of one chapter involved in this undirected reference. In cut computations, this chapter is considered together with the paired chapter to determine if the reference crosses a division.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a cross-reference: the identifier of the other chapter involved in this undirected reference. The pair (chapter_a, chapter_b) denotes a single cross-reference whose contribution to a cut depends on whether the two chapters lie on opposite sides of a division in the ordering.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct film scenes that must be placed once on the single continuous timeline; this is the size of the ordering you will produce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of narrative links (connections) between scenes; each link represents a plot thread or relationship that can cross an edit boundary if its two scenes are separated in the timeline.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (labels) for each scene available to place on the timeline; these are the items you will permute to minimize the maximum number of links crossing any cut.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a narrative link: the identifier of the first scene involved in this link. Together with 'scene_b' it defines an undirected connection between two scenes.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same narrative link: the identifier of the second scene involved. The pair (scene_a, scene_b) denotes a link whose crossing count contributes to cut sizes when the two scenes lie on opposite sides of a timeline boundary.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of players to be arranged in a single continuous rotation. This is the length of the lineup; every player must appear exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct on-field interaction pairs (duos) between players. Each pair is an undirected relationship whose members we prefer to keep together across any substitution point.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of player identifiers (names or IDs) that must be placed into the rotation. These are the items to be permuted so that substitution breaks split as few interacting pairs as possible.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an interacting duo: the identifier of the first player in this pair. Together with 'player_b' this defines a duo whose edge is counted when a substitution point separates them in the rotation.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the interacting duo: the identifier of the second player in this pair. The duo (player_a, player_b) is undirected — splitting them across any break increases that break's split-duo count by one.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exhibitor booths that must be placed once each in a single straight sequence along the aisle. This is the size of the permutation you will produce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of partnership corridors (undirected connections) between booths. These corridors are the links that can cross an aisle position and contribute to cut sizes.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of booth identifiers (names or IDs) corresponding to each exhibitor. Each identifier must appear exactly once in the final linear ordering along the aisle.

edge_item_fields.name: u
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a partnership corridor: the identifier of the first booth that the corridor connects. Together with the other endpoint, it defines an undirected corridor between two booths.

edge_item_fields.name: v
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a partnership corridor: the identifier of the second booth that the corridor connects. A corridor (booth_endpoint_1, booth_endpoint_2) contributes to cut counts when its endpoints lie on opposite sides of an aisle position in the ordering.
